summary: Two reported defects, both real, both invisible to the existing tests. FIRST: `isDisabled` had never had any visual effect. Base UI's Tab renders `aria-disabled="true"` and `data-disabled` and deliberately never sets the native `disabled` attribute — so the tab stays focusable and announceable, the same choice Calendar makes for unavailable dates — which meant every `disabled:` class in the component matched nothing. A disabled tab painted identically to an enabled one, same ink and same pointer cursor, in both schemes. The refusal worked, so the behaviour test passed; only the appearance was missing, which is the half no behaviour test could see. Now `aria-disabled:`, asserted as a DIFFERENCE from the enabled tab beside it. SECOND: the selected tab used `--ui-bg-sunken`, which measured 1.10:1 against the track in dark — 'recessed' is a RELATIVE role and the surface scale inverts between schemes, so below the surface there is room on a light page and almost none on a dark one. A new `--ui-bg-selected` role steps AWAY from the surface in whichever direction the scheme reads: light is pinned to the drawn neutral so nothing moves there, and dark goes from 1.10 to 1.68. A resolver test asserts the separation across every stress seed, in both schemes.
